goal.what: Whoever builds or changes lane, a person or an AI, derives each part's specification from this document and implements it on the same framework and principles, so lane gives the developer AI the UX in dev/lane/ux.md whatever the implementation.
grounds: architecture.json purpose
dev/lane/ux.md: O1 and O2

decisions.what: How does lane deliver its UX, in a few sentences?
decisions.decided: lay.py turns each rule of a proposal into a sentence in a step and a check of it, and puts the checks into the plugin as one check script; Claude Code runs it on each tool call and end of work of a subagent with rules; it stops each break with the sentence and tells the orchestrator each move.
grounds: dev/lane/ux.md:40-88: the two paths
plugins/lane/README.md:112-117

decisions.what: Which principles does lane take from the project, and which not?
decisions.decided: It follows dev/architecture.md's principles, except those about an orchestrator and its roles, as lay.py is run by the developer AI and the check script runs inside other plugins.
grounds: dev/architecture.md#principles
lane has no subagent of its own: plugins/lane holds no agents/

decisions.what: What makes a stopped subagent go back to its step?
decisions.decided: Principle: the check shows the step again, the rule's sentence after the plugin's name.
grounds: dev/lane/ux.md KR1.3
hooks/lane/hook.py:163, guard.py:233-234

decisions.what: How can the step and the message never differ?
decisions.decided: Principle: one wording for the step and the check, made by one piece of code from the rule's type and values.
grounds: two makers of one sentence drift; guard.py:180 and steps.py both take sentence() of the lane

decisions.what: How does only what was approved run?
decisions.decided: Principle: lay.py write writes from the file print showed, and the check script reads only what write wrote.
grounds: dev/architecture.md, The caller approves what is theirs

decisions.what: How does lane serve any plugin without its developer writing check code?
decisions.decided: Principle: lane knows no plugin; each type of rule is one check, and what differs comes as values, a run's value or an adapter.
grounds: dev/lane/ux.md KR1.4, KR2.3
the steering's T49: lane names no ccpm plugin

decisions.what: What happens where a call cannot be checked, and who is told?
decisions.decided: Principle: it is stopped; a fault is told to the subagent and the operator with who must fix it, a form lane cannot read to the subagent alone with how to write it.
grounds: dev/architecture.md, No check passes what it did not check
hook.py:125-133 tells each error to the user too; entries.py missing now does on a call as well (5af45756)

decisions.what: What does a check judge from?
decisions.decided: Principle: the check reads what the subagent did, from hook events, the record and the calls it keeps, never from what a subagent writes of its work.
grounds: an AI that says it followed a step may not have

decisions.what: What must whoever runs the plugin have of lane?
decisions.decided: Principle: the plugin needs nothing from lane; the check script is kept and run in the plugin.
grounds: plugins/lane/README.md:116-117

decisions.what: Which user stories carry the UX's steps?
decisions.decided: Four: lay.py print, lay.py write, a break stopped and an allowed call let through (O1 from the run), and the moves told and held (O2 from the run).
grounds: dev/lane/ux.md:40-88: each arrow of the two diagrams falls in one of the four

decisions.what: Which roles and stores do the stories need, each with its technology?
decisions.decided: lay.py and proposal.py; the check script of hook.py, guard.py, lanes/, called.py, moves.py and ports.py, each Python 3.9; the adapter, a Python 3 script; stores Proposal, Test cases, Plugin files, Calls kept, Record.
grounds: dev/lane/components.svg, read as source
the files exist under plugins/lane/scripts and hooks/lane

decisions.what: Which role alone decides each point?
decisions.decided: lay.py alone writes into the plugin; proposal.py alone accepts a proposal; hook.py alone speaks hook JSON; guard.py alone picks the checks, each lanes/ module alone what breaks its rule; called.py alone keeps calls; moves.py alone the next move; ports.py alone reads a plugin's text.
grounds: dev/lane/architecture.md:88-98 before this pass, checked against the modules

decisions.what: Which choices of the components would a builder question?
decisions.decided: Hooks on subagents only, as a hook is not told which skill runs; called.py keeps calls itself, as Claude Code may write a result after the next call's hooks; an adapter is a script run, not imported, so lay.py up replaces the check script without touching it.
grounds: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks: agent_type is given for subagents

decisions.what: How do the data join?
decisions.decided: The data model figure: Proposal gives Rules and a Flow, Flow holds Backs, Step holds Rules laid, Hook entry runs on Event, Kept call holds Answer, with crow's-foot ends.
grounds: dev/lane/data-model.svg: seventeen boxes, twenty-two relations named, read as source

decisions.what: What sequence does each story follow?
decisions.decided: One Mermaid sequence for each story; the flow's runs to the UX's end: lead's early end held, reviewer's `more` sending it back to move 1, the flow done and lead let end.
grounds: the flow's sequence before this pass stopped at lead's early end, short of dev/lane/ux.md:84-88
moves.py:105-115; follow_flow.py:22-34 lets the end through once none is due

decisions.what: Which choices of the sequences would a builder question?
decisions.decided: A start counts once its subagent has ended, foreground or background; the move is told as context, costing no call; an answer sends work back only on a line that is the word.
grounds: plugins/lane/docs/flow.md, What the orchestrator is told and How lane reads the answers

decisions.what: Where does each role run, and how is lane started?
decisions.decided: The developer AI's computer runs lay.py and the adapter on its test cases; the computer where the plugin runs runs the check script, one process for each event, with Calls kept in the system's temporary folder and Claude Code's record; lay.py is run as python3 <installPath>/scripts/lay.py, the check script through the plugin's hook entries.
grounds: dev/lane/deployment.svg, read as source
called.py:52 keeps calls under tempfile.gettempdir()

decisions.what: Which choices of the deployment would a builder question?
decisions.decided: Python 3.9 and the standard library only, and each hook's command checks for python3 in sh first; calls kept in the temporary folder as they mean nothing after the subagent ends; in the ccpm marketplace hooks/lane/ is a link, elsewhere a copy with VERSION.
grounds: entries.py:42
plugins/turn/hooks/lane -> ../../lane/hooks/lane
placed.py:60-82 writes and reads VERSION

decisions.what: Where does each file lie?
decisions.decided: The directory tree as the files lie: plugins/lane/scripts for lay.py and proposal.py, hooks/lane for the check script, dev/lane for documents, tests and trials, .lane/<yyyymmdd>-<plugin>/ for proposals, the temporary folder for calls kept.
grounds: every file the tree names exists, checked by ls on 2026-11-01

decisions.what: Which tests cover each deployment unit?
decisions.decided: The lay.py and hook processes by unit and integration tests; lane with a plugin by end-to-end trials; empty cells footnoted.
grounds: dev/architecture.md#test

decisions.what: What do the tests make real and fake, and when do they pass?
decisions.decided: Unit and integration tests fake Claude Code as JSON events, a record file and a claude script on PATH, and pass when all pass; trials run Claude Code on copies, passing in three runs of three.
grounds: an AI that goes back once may go round the rule the next time

decisions.what: Why are the two processes weighed heaviest?
decisions.decided: A failure writes what no one approved, or lets a break through in a plugin whose operator never sees lane.
grounds: D5, D9

decisions.what: What keeps the document true while a role changes inside?
decisions.decided: Each line says a role's responsibility, a relation or a choice with its reason, not a function or a field; message texts stay in docs/flow.md and docs/lanes.md.
grounds: architecture.json Q15

decisions.what: How are the code's own names, lane and guard, said?
decisions.decided: Said once under Principles: the code and docs/lanes.md call a rule a lane and the check script the guard.
grounds: plugins/lane/docs/flow.md: "the guard, lane's code in your plugin's hooks/lane/"
renaming them is T47's, as the steering notes
